body: Founder: 'publish blog in traditional Chinese and sans[k]rit' then 'then a followup in ceremonial Japanese'. Published two posts reflecting on the just-shipped SKULDMARK-25 identifier: (1) '名色 nāmarūpa' (Emily Prime) -- Traditional Chinese body framed through the real Buddhist doctrinal term nāmarūpa (name-and-form, the pair a SKULDMARK identifier and the real instrument it names correspond to); Sanskrit limited to the one verified term नामरूप plus its known gloss, explicitly not attempting full Sanskrit prose since that couldn't be guaranteed correct. (2) '謹告 — SKULDMARKの制定について' (EINHORN_INDUSTRIAL) -- a short formal-announcement-register (謹告) Japanese piece proclaiming the release, again flagged in-post as an attempt at ceremonial register rather than a claim of verified classical grammar. Both live (200 over public HTTPS), footer links added, OKEMILY commit 1d9dbbc.
title: Published SKULDMARK follow-up posts: Chinese/Sanskrit + ceremonial Japanese
